nodes.statement: Four ternary coordinate fibres give the affine plane of order three. Deleting one direction recovers all 27 labelled Pappus edges.
The nine line disjunctions cost 18 gates in the one-free-NOT model.
Can one selected-edge output be realized with eight AND gates and free OR gates on 18 independent inputs?
Gaussian and Eisenstein multiplication have cycle types 2+2 and 1+3 on the four deletion directions.
Two marked Klein groups lie in a common group of order 48. One translation direction has trace −8 and four have trace zero.
The marked Albert cubic has stabilizer of order four and an orbit of twelve in the octad group.
The common 18-dimensional rational summand needs at least 24 points in a permutation realization.
The marked octad traces give the cubic for the Erdős–Straus denominators. The octonion cubic varies within a single trace fibre.
Twenty-one Albert projectors have fourteen orthogonal triples. Their intersections recover Fano incidence and the two six-sheet actions.
Exactly 1,320 planes in the extended ternary Golay code admit the simultaneous quadratic and quartic null lift modulo nine.
Rationally equivalent linear transports give edge functions with optimal circuit sizes 436 and 437. The gap grows by one per copy.
Point and line transport in the plane of order four preserves the rational metric and unit, but its two subdivided covers need 1,968 and 1,967 gates.
The four roots of the tetrahedral quartic are halves of a rational point at j=2304 in the six-sphere family.
The mod-three action at the same curve has group GL₂(3), giving a conjugacy class for lambency-six twining.
The marked cyclic cover and the lambency-six modular curve have a connected common cover of genus 25.
The normalized invariant of the multiplicity-four Albanese torus on the parameter disc equals the graded dimension series of the moonshine module at its specified nome.
The primes admitting both a rational half and a rational order-three direction have density 15/32.
The twelve level-six markings over j=2304 form one Galois orbit. The normalized Fricke trace over them is 1,500.
A cubic rational map sends the level-six parameter to the Eisenstein parameter and preserves the ordinary elliptic invariant.
The two elliptic models differ by the square class −2 at the marked arithmetic point. Projective directions survive, and signed traces acquire the twisting character.
On the admissible level-six parameter line, the K3 point-count formula is a signed elliptic symmetric square with quadratic character given by x+9.
The six distinguished two-torsion points of the marked Jacobian carry the same three paired orbits as the six ramification points of its Klein-four period cover.
Halved squared inertia yields the marked cusp map (2,3,3). Its only permutation symmetry is the identity, so no fibration automorphism cycles the three exceptional fibres.
The projective level-four cover and the level-six line have a connected common cover over their shared level-two parameter. Its genus is three and its degree over the ordinary j-line is 96.
Two entries of the lambency-six twined shadow matrix give the cardinality of the elliptic three-torsion fixed by Frobenius and by its negative.
The first shadow entry determines the corresponding K3 point count modulo three once its quadratic character is supplied. The character is trivial on good points of the conductor period cover.
The genus-three common cover has Jacobian rationally isogenous to two copies of one elliptic curve and its minus-one quadratic twist. This determines every good finite-field point count.
The common elliptic invariant is nonintegral, excluding complex multiplication. The genus-three Jacobian thus admits no origin-preserving automorphism of order seven even up to isogeny.
The first pair of sections tends to the square elliptic curve. Its images tend to discriminant minus sixteen. The other conductor image heights diverge at distinct rates.

nodes.statement: With the same integral monodromy the three conductor image periods can be taken as 2i, iε²/2 and iε. Their pairwise isogenies are characterized by rationality of ε², ε and ε³ respectively.
A rational half and a cyclic order-six subgroup coexist on a set of primes of density 5/96.
A weighted selection of auxiliary primes for specified characteristics gives a batch of at most one plus the base-r logarithm of its size.
An additive lift of both null equations modulo nine gives the polarized dimension bound in characteristic three.
Three full antidiagonals require at least (3/2)^k reusable signings on a family of balanced deletions.
On a Pfaffian input graph, a histogram with at most three core labels and t exceptional occurrences can be counted in 2^t times polynomial time.
A relative trace makes an expanded inverse exponentially long even for some systems with a constant-degree refutation.
For a supplied cycle code, an odd-prime common valuation reduces to a minimum-weight T-join.
A supplied planar cycle-code realization gives individual coefficients at every modulus via a Pfaffian.
One specified block of a coefficient on general cycle-code inputs encodes the permanent of a binary matrix.
Fixed-width CNF with a supplied small affine boundary admits the stated subexponential signed weighted count.
The rank-four Hecke order has generic rank 114 and needs at least 126 module generators at the exceptional point. Two length-ten words survive modulo all shorter words.
The exact adapted-lattice quotient follows from three finite data conditions. The regular-representation lower bound has a standalone checker.
The Hasse coefficient gives a sharp generic lower bound on vanishing order along repeated padding in positive characteristic.
Hitchin’s quartic and one derivative freely generate a width-seven plethysm ray with multiplicity k+1 in degree 6k.
The first tail of that ray contributes twice in one symmetric-algebra factor. Its complete stable Foulkes coefficient is 2,097.
Changing a single symmetric pair of displacements changes an explicit simplex-like Kronecker coefficient from a binomial coefficient to zero.
A supplied genus-g cycle code within binary subspace distance k gives individual coefficients in 2^k 4^g times polynomial time.
Certified periods of the decoded Boolean predicate remove characters from the sparse-gcd probe and shrink its required fibre degree.
On an ordinary Artin–Schreier family the first J extension counts are identical to the projective line while the scalar of a local Weil operator determines the number of witnesses.
The same random local Boolean encoding has linear degree in polynomial calculus over every field and survives linearly many rounds of real Lasserre.
Five field maps locate 60 proposed connections across algebra and combinatorics, moonshine, algebraic geometry, arithmetic and Hodge theory. Each entry identifies its targets and the step required.
